title: Move Zeros to end
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Move all zeros to the end while preserving the order of non-zero elements.
intuition: This is a stable partition. A write pointer collects non-zeros in order; whatever is left over is filled with zeros — or swap as you go to do it in one pass.

approaches.title: Brute: build a new list
approaches.idea: Copy non-zeros, then pad with zeros.
approaches.code:
def move_zeros_extra(a: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    out = [x for x in a if x != 0]
    out += [0] * (len(a) - len(out))
    a[:] = out
    return a

approaches.title: Optimal: swap with the first zero
approaches.idea: j points at the leftmost zero; every non-zero found after it swaps in.
approaches.whyWorks: a[0..j) holds non-zeros in original order; a[j..i) is all zeros.

commonMistakes: Breaking stability by swapping with the array end
patternRecognition: Stable in-place partition -> write pointer (same skeleton as Dutch-flag one-sided)
followUps: Move zeros to the front instead
Partition around an arbitrary pivot, stably
interviewInsight: They watch for stability. Two-pointer swapping keeps it; sorting-by-key does not, for free.
